mainTopic: רבי יהודה on a second fetus (חומרא, not קולא); the sliding-scale offering (קרבן עולה ויורד) and why the poorest offering is worth a פרוטה; and the start of the משנה on the שפחה חרופה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing רב אשי's proof that רבי יהודה counts a second fetus only to be strict (חומרא), never to be lenient (קולא). A second ברייתא about the 'six days' of purification leads to the same result, and the גמרא accepts it. Then a new משנה lists five cases that bring a sliding-scale offering (קרבן עולה ויורד): two kinds of false oath, טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, a יולדת, and a מצורע. Two ברייתות sort these cases by how many wealth levels each has and by which offerings are swapped at the poorer level. One of them teaches that the very poor person's flour offering (עשירית האיפה) can be worth as little as a פרוטה. The גמרא works out the prices step by step, starting from a lamb worth a סלע. After two answers fail to give exactly one פרוטה, רבא's calculation from the יולדת gives three-quarters of a פרוטה. The ברייתא rounds this up, because it is not proper to bring ה׳ less than a פרוטה. Finally a new משנה begins listing how a שפחה חרופה differs from the other עריות in punishment and offering, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Finishing the first proof: only רבי יהודה allows scattered days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes רב אשי's first proof. The רבנן cannot be the author of the ברייתא about scattered days, so it must be רבי יהודה. That shows he counts the second fetus only for stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Could the רבנן hold that she counts scattered days? But the רבנן say she counts from the second birth! So it must be רבי יהודה. Learn from this that he applies the second fetus for a stringency but not for a leniency.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a proof that started just before this section. It shows that the ברייתא about 'scattered' days only fits רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say a woman who gives birth to a second fetus simply starts a fresh count from that second birth. Under their view, her days are never split up or 'scattered.' Since the ברייתא even considers scattered days, it must follow רבי יהודה. That teaches us how he treats the second fetus: it counts when it makes her stricter, but not when it would make her more lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: Scattered, non-continuous days, with the count broken up and finished later.
The second fetus or offspring, born after the first one.
She counts.
'Rather, is it not…?' This leads into the only remaining option.
A stringency, a stricter result.
A leniency, a more lenient result.

steps.confusionAlert: This step begins in the middle of a sentence. The question 'מפוזרין?' finishes a line that started just before this section. It means 'Do the רבנן even have a concept of scattered days?'

phrases.english: scattered days?
But the Rabbis say:
she counts from the second offspring!
Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda?
And learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: חוּמְרָא אִית לֵיהּ, קוּלָּא לֵית לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: he holds of it for a stringency, but not for a leniency.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a proof that began before this section.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה counts the second fetus only for stringency, not for leniency.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that considers scattered days, which can only follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: רב אשי brings a second ברייתא about the six days
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes a ברייתא on the 'sixty and six days' of a woman who gave birth to a girl. It teaches that the six days must be continuous, just like the sixty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי also said: Come and hear. 'And six days': you might think they can be either continuous or scattered. So the פסוק says 'sixty.' Just as the sixty are all continuous, so too the six are all continuous.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings another source to prove the same point. This step only quotes the ברייתא; the next step will figure out who its author is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raises the idea that the six days might be 'scattered.' It then rejects that idea by comparing them to the sixty days, which run in a row. What matters for the proof is that the ברייתא even considers scattered days as an option.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore. This brings an additional proof.
'One might think.' The ברייתא raises a possibility it will reject.
Continuous, one day right after another.
'The פסוק teaches.' This brings the wording that settles the question.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: And Rav Ashi further said: Come and hear:
"And six days"
One might think, whether continuous or scattered?
The verse states: "sixty",
just as the sixty are all continuous,
so too the six are all continuous.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second, parallel source for the same conclusion as Step 1.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה's view that the second fetus counts only for stringency.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'ששת ימים' that considers continuous versus scattered days.

steps.title: Who wrote this ברייתא? Not the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the author is. It rules out the רבנן, because under their view a fresh count starts at the second birth, so scattered days never come up.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this? If you say the רבנן, do the רבנן even have scattered days? But the רבנן say she counts from the second offspring!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the ברייתא, and it rejects the רבנן as the author. This sets up the conclusion in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The logic is the same as in Step 1. For the רבנן, the second birth simply resets the count, so the question of scattered days could never come up. A ברייתא that even asks about it must follow someone else.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is it? This asks who authored the teaching.
If you say. This proposes an option in order to test it.
'Do they hold of…?' A rhetorical question that expects 'no.'

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
If you say the Rabbis,
do the Rabbis hold of scattered days at all?
But the Rabbis say:
she counts from the second offspring!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַנִּי? אִלֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out who authored the ברייתא quoted in Step 2.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא is the author of the ברייתא about the six days?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Not the רבנן, because for them the second birth restarts the count.

steps.title: So it must be רבי יהודה: stringency yes, leniency no
steps.stepSummary: Since the author is not the רבנן, it must be רבי יהודה. That shows he applies the second fetus only for stringency.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't it רבי יהודה? Can we learn from this that he holds of the second fetus for a stringency but not for a leniency?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concludes the ברייתא follows רבי יהודה. It then proposes what this teaches about his view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהודה, the second birth does not wipe out the first count, so the question of 'scattered' leftover days can even come up. The ברייתא then rules those scattered days out. This shows that for him the second fetus counts when it makes things stricter, and not when it would be lenient.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not Rabbi Yehuda?
And can we learn from it:

phrases.aramaic: חוּמְרָא אִית לֵיהּ, קוּלָּא לֵית לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: he holds of it for a stringency, but not for a leniency?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו רַבִּי יְהוּדָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion that follows from ruling out the רבנן in Step 3.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהודה: the second fetus counts for חומרא, not for קולא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ששת ימים ברייתא, which can only follow רבי יהודה.

steps.title: The גמרא accepts the proof
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: yes, learn it from here.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, learn it from this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts רב אשי's proof as correct. This closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שמע מינה' confirms the proposed conclusion. It is now established that רבי יהודה applies the second fetus only to be strict, never to be lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Learn from it.' The גמרא is agreeing that the proof works.

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יהודה, a second fetus counts only when it makes things stricter (חומרא), not when it would make things more lenient (קולא). For the רבנן, the count simply restarts from the second birth.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Confirms the inference proposed in Step 4.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה: חומרא אית ליה, קולא לית ליה. He counts the second fetus only for stringency.

steps.title: New משנה: who brings a sliding-scale offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists the five cases that bring a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.simpleTranslation: These bring a sliding-scale offering: for hearing the voice of an oath, for a rash spoken oath, for making the מקדש or its holy foods impure, a woman after childbirth, and a מצורע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists the cases that bring a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן עולה ויורד changes with a person's wealth: a rich person brings an animal, and a poorer person brings birds or flour. The משנה names five cases: two about oaths, one about impurity and the מקדש, a יולדת, and a מצורע.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה. This marks the start of a new משנה.
A sliding-scale offering that goes up or down depending on what a person can afford.
Literally, 'hearing the voice': falsely swearing you have no testimony to give.
A spoken oath that was violated or false.
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while impure.
A person with צרעת, here at the end of his purification.

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה sets the topic for the coming סוגיות, which explain how each of these cases brings a sliding-scale offering.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
These bring a sliding-scale offering:
for hearing the voice of an oath,
phrases.notes: This is someone who heard an oath asking him to testify and falsely swore he knew nothing.

phrases.english: and for an utterance of the lips,
and for impurity of the Temple and its sacred foods,
and a woman after childbirth, and a leper.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ אֵלּוּ מְבִיאִין קׇרְבָּן עוֹלֶה וְיוֹרֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five cases bring a קרבן עולה ויורד: שמיעת קול, ביטוי שפתיים, טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, יולדת, and מצורע.

steps.title: Three Levels of Money for a Sliding-Scale Offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says some people bring this offering at a rich or poor level, and some go down to a very poor level.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Some people bring the offering at a poor level or a rich level. Some bring at a poor level. And some bring at a very poor level.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה by quoting a ברייתא. It lists the money levels at which a קרבן עולה ויורד can be brought. This general line sets up the details that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קרבן עולה ויורד changes with the owner's wealth. This ברייתא shows that not every case has the same number of levels. Some stop at the poor level, and some go one step lower, to very poor.

keyTerms.meaning: A sliding-scale offering that goes up or down with the owner's wealth
Poverty, the poor level
Wealth, the rich level
Extreme poverty, the lowest level

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Sages taught:
There is one who brings in poverty and in wealth,
and there is one who brings in poverty,
and there is one who brings in extreme poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: תנו רבנן יש מביא בדלות ועשירות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה that listed the five cases of a קרבן עולה ויורד.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sliding-scale offerings come in different numbers of levels: some have rich and poor, and some also have a very poor level.

steps.title: Which Cases Fit Which Levels
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא matches each case to its levels. A יולדת and a מצורע have rich and poor levels. The oath cases and the טומאה cases go down to very poor.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman after childbirth brings at a poor or rich level. A leper brings at a poor level. For the hearing of the voice, the utterance of the lips, and the defiling of the מקדש or its holy foods, one brings at a poor level and at a very poor level.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now names which case belongs to each level from the general line in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The main point is the split: a יולדת and a מצורע never go below the poor level of birds. The three cases of שמיעת הקול, ביטוי שפתים, and טומאת מקדש וקדשיו can go one level lower, to a flour offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has given birth
A person with צרעת who is being purified
Falsely swearing that one has no testimony to give
A spoken oath that was broken by mistake
Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Even though the line says the מצורע brings 'in poverty', he also has a rich level in the Torah. The point is that he, like the יולדת, never goes down to extreme poverty.

phrases.english: A woman after childbirth brings in poverty or in wealth.
A leper brings in poverty.
The hearing of the voice and the utterance of the lips
and the defiling of the Temple or its holy foods,
bring in poverty and in extreme poverty.

steps.triggerLanguage: יולדת מביאה בדלות ועשירות
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the cases behind the general levels named in Step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יולדת and מצורע: rich and poor levels only. The oath cases and the טומאה cases: down to extreme poverty.

steps.title: Four Swap Patterns, and the Value of the Flour Offering
steps.stepSummary: A second ברייתא lists four ways a cheaper offering replaces a richer one. From this it learns that a עשירית האיפה can be worth just a פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: Some bring one offering instead of one. Some bring two instead of two. Some bring two instead of one. Some bring one instead of two. From here you learn that a tenth of an איפה can be worth as little as a פרוטה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a second ברייתא that looks at the same cases differently: how many offerings are swapped at the lower level. It states the four patterns first and draws a lesson. The next step matches each pattern to a case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first ברייתא counted levels. This one counts what gets swapped. From these swaps the ברייתא learns that the very poor person's flour offering can be worth as little as a פרוטה. The גמרא works out exactly how in Steps 11–22, finally using the יולדת's swap.

keyTerms.meaning: Instead of, in place of
A tenth of an איפה of flour, the flour offering of the very poor
The smallest coin that counts as having value
From here you learn, which marks a lesson drawn from what was just said

phrases.english: It is taught in another ברייתא:
There is one who brings one instead of one,
there is one who brings two instead of two,
there is one who brings two instead of one,
there is one who brings one instead of two.
From here you learn
that the tenth of an ephah can be worth a peruta.

steps.triggerLanguage: תניא אידך יש מביא אחד תחת אחד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second way of sorting the same cases, by the swap pattern instead of the number of levels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There are four swap patterns, and the flour offering of a tenth of an איפה can be worth as little as a פרוטה.

steps.title: Matching Each Swap Pattern to Its Case
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא explains each pattern: the יולדת swaps one for one, the מצורע two for two, the oath and טומאה cases two for one, and extreme poverty one for two.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman after childbirth brings one instead of one: one young bird, plus a bird in place of the lamb. A leper brings two young birds instead of two lambs. For the hearing of the voice, the utterance of the lips, and the defiling of the מקדש or its holy foods, one brings two young birds instead of one female lamb. In extreme poverty, one brings a tenth of an איפה instead of two young birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now names the case behind each of the four swap patterns from the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת always brings a bird חטאת, so only her lamb עולה is swapped: one for one. A מצורע swaps his two lambs for two birds. In the oath and טומאה cases, one female lamb is replaced by two birds, and in extreme poverty those two birds are replaced by one flour offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A young bird, a young dove or pigeon
A male lamb
A female lamb
A bird

steps.whatToRemember: Two ברייתות sort the same five cases. By levels: יולדת and מצורע have rich and poor; the oath and טומאה cases also have very poor. By swaps: יולדת one for one, מצורע two for two, oath and טומאה two for one, and very poor one for two. From these swaps the ברייתא learns that a עשירית האיפה can be worth a פרוטה.

phrases.english: A woman after childbirth brings one instead of one:
one young bird, and a bird instead of the lamb.

phrases.aramaic: מְצוֹרָע – שְׁתֵּי פְרִידִין תַּחַת שְׁנֵי כְבָשִׂים,
phrases.english: A leper brings two young birds instead of two lambs.
The hearing of the voice and the utterance of the lips
and the defiling of the Temple or its holy foods:

phrases.aramaic: מְבִיאִין שְׁתֵּי פְרִידִין תַּחַת כִּבְשָׂה אַחַת,
phrases.english: one brings two young birds instead of one female lamb,
and in extreme poverty one brings
a tenth of an ephah instead of two young birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: יולדת מביאה אחת תחת אחת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Names the case behind each of the four swap patterns stated in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יולדת: one for one. מצורע: two for two. Oath and טומאה cases: two birds for one female lamb. Extreme poverty: one flour offering for two birds.

steps.title: Where do we know a עשירית האיפה can be worth one פרוטה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the ברייתא that a עשירית האיפה can be worth a פרוטה, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא teaches: from here you learn that a עשירית האיפה can be worth one פרוטה. How do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up the last line of the ברייתא from step 9 and asks how we know it. This sets up a long proof that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא claimed that the very poor person's flour offering can cost as little as a פרוטה. The גמרא wants to see the actual pricing logic behind that claim. The next steps build the answer piece by piece.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an ephah of flour, the flour offering brought by the very poor
The smallest coin
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: It teaches: from here you learn
that a tenth of an ephah can be worth a peruta.
From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of a claim the ברייתא made in step 9
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The basis for saying a עשירית האיפה can be worth only a פרוטה

steps.title: A pledge of one סלע means bringing a lamb
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that someone who pledges a סלע for the altar brings a lamb, because only a lamb costs a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: if someone says, 'I take upon myself a סלע for the altar,' he brings a lamb, because nothing offered on the altar costs a סלע except a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by setting a price: a lamb is worth one סלע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: To figure out the cheapest offering, the גמרא starts from the top. The rich offering in these cases is a lamb, and this ברייתא sets its price at one סלע. Every step down will be measured from this number.

keyTerms.meaning: A silver coin worth four דינרים
A lamb, the rich person's offering
'I take upon myself', the wording of a pledge

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
One who says: "I take upon myself an offering worth a sela for the altar"
brings a lamb,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאֵין דָּבָר קָרֵב בְּסֶלַע אֶלָּא כֶּבֶשׂ.
phrases.english: since nothing offered on the altar is worth a sela except a lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתָנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A lamb is worth one סלע, which is the starting price for the calculation

steps.title: Proof from the ram of an אשם that a lamb costs one סלע
steps.stepSummary: The Torah requires the ram of an אשם to be worth 'shekels', meaning two סלעים. So a younger lamb, in its first year, is worth one סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know a lamb is worth a סלע? The Torah says 'a ram for an אשם, worth silver shekels', which is two סלעים. So a lamb in its first year must be worth one סלע. And we know the offering is a first-year lamb, because the פסוק says 'a lamb in its first year'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how we know a lamb costs one סלע, and proves it from the Torah's price for the ram of an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'shekels' means at least two, so the older ram is worth two סלעים. A younger lamb in its first year is then worth half, one סלע. The פסוק about the יולדת shows that the offering here is exactly this first-year lamb.

keyTerms.meaning: The ram brought as a guilt offering
Silver shekels; the plural means at least two
It follows from this
A lamb in its first year

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
Since the Merciful One said: "a ram for a guilt offering, worth silver shekels",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 5:15. 'Shekels' is plural, so the ram must be worth at least two סלעים.

phrases.english: it follows that a year-old lamb is worth a sela,
since it is written: "a lamb in its first year".

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי? מִדְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the price stated in step 12 with a פסוק
steps.raayaObject: That a first-year lamb is worth one סלע
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 5:15 (the ram of an אשם is worth shekels) and ויקרא 12:6 (a first-year lamb)

steps.title: The birds cost a quarter dinar
steps.stepSummary: A משנה reports that the price of a pair of birds once fell to a quarter דינר, which is one-sixteenth of a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we learned in a משנה: that day the price of bird pairs stood at a quarter of a דינר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now prices the poor person's offering, the pair of birds, at a quarter דינר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A סלע is four דינרים, so a quarter דינר is one-sixteenth of a סלע. This shows that the poor offering can be just one-sixteenth of the rich offering. That ratio is the key to the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Pairs of birds, the poor person's offering
A quarter of a silver דינר

steps.confusionAlert: The quarter here is a quarter of a דינר, not a quarter of a סלע. Since a סלע has four דינרים, this works out to one-sixteenth of a סלע.

phrases.english: And we learned in a mishna:
The bird pairs stood that day at a quarter of a dinar.
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה earlier in the מסכת (דף ח), where the price of birds dropped on one day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן: עָמְדוּ קִינִּין בּוֹ בַּיּוֹם בְּרִבְעָתַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the price of the poor offering to go with the lamb's price
steps.raayaObject: That the poor offering can be one-sixteenth of the rich offering
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה on דף ח about the price of bird pairs

steps.title: The same one-sixteenth discount applies to the very poor
steps.stepSummary: Since the Torah lets the poor bring one-sixteenth of the rich offering, it also lets the very poor bring one-sixteenth of the poor offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the Torah had mercy on the poor person and let his offering be one-sixteenth of the rich offering, the Torah also has mercy on the very poor person and lets his offering be one-sixteenth of the poor offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reasons that the 'one-sixteenth' ratio repeats one more level down, for the very poor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rich-to-poor drop is one-sixteenth (a סלע down to a quarter דינר). The גמרא assumes the Torah's mercy works the same way going from poor to very poor. So the very poor offering is one-sixteenth of a quarter דינר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah had mercy, meaning it made the offering cheaper
Poverty, the poor level
Wealth, the rich level
Extreme poverty, the very poor level
One-sixteenth

phrases.english: And since the Merciful One had mercy on the poor level
letting it be one-sixteenth of the rich level,
the Merciful One has mercy on the very poor level
letting it be one-sixteenth of the poor level.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּחָס רַחֲמָנָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּדַלּוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the one-sixteenth ratio found in steps 12–14 and applies it one level lower
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The very poor offering is one-sixteenth of the value of the poor offering

steps.title: Working out the numbers: three פרוטות
steps.stepSummary: The poor offering is a quarter דינר, which is 48 פרוטות. One-sixteenth of that is 3 פרוטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, how much is the poor offering worth? A quarter דינר. How many פרוטות are in a quarter? Forty-eight. So how much is one-sixteenth of the poor offering? Three פרוטות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does the arithmetic to find the value of the very poor offering in פרוטות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A quarter דינר equals 48 פרוטות. Taking one-sixteenth of 48 gives 3 פרוטות. So far the very poor offering comes out to three פרוטות, not yet the single פרוטה the ברייתא spoke of.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarter of a דינר
פרוטות, the smallest coins

steps.confusionAlert: The result here is three פרוטות, not one. Don't think the proof is finished; the ברייתא's claim of one פרוטה still has to be reached.
steps.whatToRemember: Lamb = one סלע; birds = a quarter דינר (one-sixteenth); very poor = one-sixteenth of that, which is 3 פרוטות.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, דַּלּוּת כְּמָה הָוְיָא – רִיבְעָא,
phrases.english: If so, how much is the poor level worth? A quarter,

phrases.aramaic: וּכְמָה פְּרִיטֵי בְּרִיבְעָא – אַרְבָּעִים וּתְמָנְיָא פְּרִיטֵי,
phrases.english: and how many perutot are in a quarter? Forty-eight perutot,

phrases.aramaic: חַד מִשֵּׁית עֲשַׂר כְּמָה הָוֵי דְּדַלּוּת –
phrases.english: how much is one-sixteenth of the poor level?
Three perutot.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, דַּלּוּת כְּמָה הָוְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the ratio from step 15 into an actual number
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By this calculation, the very poor offering is worth three פרוטות

steps.title: The ברייתא says one פרוטה, but the math gave three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says the עשירית האיפה can be worth one פרוטה, when the math from steps 15–16 made it 3 פרוטות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא says: from here you learn that the tenth of an איפה can be worth a פרוטה. Why a פרוטה? You said it is the offering of extreme poverty, and that it is one-sixteenth of the poor offering. We worked that out to be three פרוטות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own earlier calculation. The math said 3 פרוטות, but the ברייתא says only 1 פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15–16 said the very poor bring 1/16 of the poor offering. The poor offering is 48 פרוטות, so 1/16 of it is 3 פרוטות. The ברייתא's number of one פרוטה does not match.

keyTerms.meaning: A tenth of an איפה of flour, the offering of the very poorest person
Extreme poverty, the poorest level
Poverty, the middle level (the person brings birds)
The smallest coin
Why?

phrases.english: That which it teaches: From here you learn
that the tenth of an ephah can be worth a peruta,
why a peruta?

phrases.aramaic: הָאָמְרַתְּ: עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה דַּלֵּי דַּלּוּת הוּא,
phrases.english: Didn't you say: the tenth of an ephah is for extreme poverty,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרַתְּ חַד מִשֵּׁית סְרֵי דְּדַלּוּת הוּא,
phrases.english: and you said it is one-sixteenth of the poverty offering,
which we calculated to be three perutot!

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי פְּרוּטָה? הָאָמְרַתְּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the 3-פרוטות result of step 16 to attack the ברייתא's figure of one פרוטה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that the עשירית האיפה can be worth one פרוטה

steps.title: The תנא learns from the יולדת
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the תנא sets the price of the poor offering using a יולדת, who brings one bird instead of a lamb. One bird is 1/32 of a lamb.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא learns from a woman after childbirth. She brings one bird in place of a lamb, and a bird is one thirty-second of a lamb.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing how much the poor offering is worth. It uses one bird, not a pair of birds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יולדת who is poor brings one bird in place of the lamb. A pair of birds costs 48 פרוטות, so one bird costs 24 פרוטות. That is 1/32 of a lamb worth a סלע, so the poor level drops from 48 to 24 פרוטות.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who has given birth and brings offerings
A single bird (one of a pair)
A lamb
One thirty-second

phrases.english: The tanna learns it from a woman after childbirth,
who brings one bird in place of a lamb,
which is one thirty-second of a lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא מִיּוֹלֶדֶת יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer step 17 by lowering the price of the poor offering.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source for the base value
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The poor offering is a pair of birds, worth 48 פרוטות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The poor offering is one bird, worth 24 פרוטות (1/32 of a lamb).

steps.title: Even so, it only comes to a פרוטה and a half
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows the first answer is not enough. 1/16 of 24 פרוטות is still a פרוטה and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: But so far, how much is extreme poverty? One-sixteenth of poverty, which we learned from the lamb and the ram. So we still only get a פרוטה and a half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer of step 18. The number still does not come out to one פרוטה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 1/16 ratio still comes from the ram and the lamb (step 13). 1/16 of 24 פרוטות is 1.5 פרוטות, not 1. So the answer of step 18 does not work.

keyTerms.meaning: A ram
One-sixteenth
A פרוטה and a half

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן, דַּלֵּי דַּלּוּת כְּמָה הָוֵי –
phrases.english: But until now, how much is the extreme poverty offering?
One-sixteenth of the poverty offering,
for from where is it learned? From the lamb and the ram.
So until now, it comes to a peruta and a half!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן, דַּלֵּי דַּלּוּת כְּמָה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 18's answer as not reaching one פרוטה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even with 24 פרוטות as the poor level, 1/16 of it gives 1.5 פרוטות, not 1.

steps.title: רבא: the whole ratio comes from the יולדת
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both the price and the ratio come from the יולדת. The poor bring 1/32 of the rich offering, so the very poor bring 1/32 of the poor offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: the whole thing is learned from the יולדת. Just as the Torah had pity on the poor and let them bring 1/32 of what the rich bring (that is the יולדת), so the Torah has pity on the very poor and lets them bring 1/32 of what the poor bring.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new answer. He drops the 1/16 ratio and uses 1/32 from the יולדת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the יולדת, one bird (24 פרוטות) is 1/32 of a lamb. רבא uses that same 1/32 step to go down from the poor level to the very poor level. 1/32 of 24 פרוטות is 3/4 of a פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole matter
The Torah (the Merciful One) had pity
Wealth, the rich level

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: rich to poor is 1/32 (from the יולדת), and poor to very poor is also 1/32.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: כּוּלַּהּ מִילְּתָא מִיּוֹלֶדֶת יָלֵיף,
phrases.english: Rava said: The whole matter is learned from a woman after childbirth,
and this is what he is saying:
Since the Merciful One had pity on the poor
to bring one thirty-second of the wealthy offering,
and what case is that? A woman after childbirth,

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי חָס רַחֲמָנָא עֲלֵיהּ דְּדַלֵּי דַּלּוּת
phrases.english: so too the Merciful One has pity on the extremely poor

phrases.aramaic: לְמִיהְוֵי חַד מִן תְּלָתִין וּתְרֵין בְּדַלּוּת.
phrases.english: to bring one thirty-second of the poverty offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כּוּלַּהּ מִילְּתָא מִיּוֹלֶדֶת יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the failed answer of steps 18–19 with a new ratio.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The very poor bring 1/16 of the poor offering (from ram and lamb).
steps.terutzMaskana: The very poor bring 1/32 of the poor offering (from the יולדת).

steps.title: Then it should be less than a פרוטה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that רבא's math gives 3/4 of a פרוטה, not a full פרוטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it comes to a פרוטה minus a quarter!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא's answer. Now the number is too low.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 1/32 of 24 פרוטות is 3/4 of a פרוטה. So the ברייתא should have said 3/4 of a פרוטה, not one whole פרוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Minus a quarter

phrases.aramaic: אִי הָכִי, נְכֵי רִיבְעָא דִּפְרוּטָה הָוֵי!
phrases.english: If so, it is a peruta minus a quarter!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, נְכֵי רִיבְעָא דִּפְרוּטָה הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the math of רבא's answer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 1/32 of 24 פרוטות is 3/4 of a פרוטה, which does not match the ברייתא's one פרוטה.

steps.title: Never bring less than a פרוטה to ה׳
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees the math gives 3/4 of a פרוטה, but it is rounded up. It is not proper to bring less than a פרוטה to ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is true. But it is not proper to bring less than a פרוטה to ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge's math and explains the ברייתא's number. The very poor offering is set at a full פרוטה out of respect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the strict math, 3/4 of a פרוטה would be enough. But an offering worth less than the smallest coin is not fitting for ה׳. So the minimum becomes one פרוטה, which matches the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Indeed, that is so
Proper conduct, the respectful way
To ה׳ (the Omnipresent)

steps.whatToRemember: The very poor person's flour offering: by the math, 3/4 of a פרוטה; in practice, at least one פרוטה, because we do not bring ה׳ less than a פרוטה.

phrases.english: Indeed so,
but it is not proper conduct
to bring less than a peruta to the Omnipresent.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא דְּלָאו אוֹרַח אַרְעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the math of step 21 and explains why the ברייתא still says one פרוטה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepts the math and adds a rule of respect
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The value should be exactly 3/4 of a פרוטה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is rounded up to one פרוטה, because it is not proper to bring ה׳ less than a פרוטה.

steps.title: The maidservant brings a different offering than other forbidden relations
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how a שפחה is different from the other עריות. It answers that she is not like them, either for punishment or for the קרבן: other עריות bring a female חטאת, and a שפחה brings a male אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: What is the difference between a maidservant and all the other forbidden relations? She is not like them, not in punishment and not in the offering. For all forbidden relations, the offering is a sin offering, but for a maidservant it is a guilt offering. For all forbidden relations, the animal is a female, but for a maidservant it is a male.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens. It asks how a שפחה is different from all other עריות and starts listing the differences.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who sins by accident with any of the עריות brings a חטאת, and a חטאת is a female animal. Someone who sins by accident with a שפחה חרופה brings an אשם instead, and an אשם is a male animal. So the type of offering and the kind of animal both change.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant who is half-free and is promised (espoused) to a Jewish slave
The forbidden relationships listed in the Torah
Punishment
Sin offering, brought from a female animal
Guilt offering, brought from a male animal
Female / male (animal)

steps.confusionAlert: The word שפחה in this משנה does not mean any maidservant. It means the special case of a שפחה חרופה from the Torah's פרשה of the אשם.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
What is the difference between a maidservant
phrases.notes: This means the espoused maidservant, the שפחה חרופה, from ויקרא 19:20.

phrases.english: and all the forbidden relations?
That she is not equal to them,
not in punishment and not in the offering.
For all the forbidden relations are with a sin offering,
and a maidservant is with a guilt offering.
All the forbidden relations are with a female animal,
and a maidservant is with a male animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה בֵּין שִׁפְחָה לְבֵין כׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the earlier discussion of the poor person's offering ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For other עריות the offering is a female חטאת. For a שפחה חרופה it is a male אשם.

steps.title: Man and woman are not treated equally with the maidservant
steps.stepSummary: For all other עריות, the man and the woman are treated the same for מלקות and for a קרבן. With a שפחה, the Torah does not treat them the same, either for מלקות or for the קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: For all forbidden relations, the man and the woman are equal for lashes and for the offering. But with a maidservant, the Torah did not make the man equal to the woman for lashes, and did not make the woman equal to the man for the offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second difference. With other עריות both people get the same treatment, but with a שפחה they do not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With other עריות, if both were warned, both get מלקות; if both sinned by accident, both bring a קרבן. With a שפחה, the man and the woman do not share the same punishment, and only the man brings the קרבן, since the woman is not made equal to him for the offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Lashes (מלקות), a punishment from בית דין
Equal; treated the same way
He (the Torah) made equal

phrases.english: In all the forbidden relations,
both the man and the woman
are equal in lashes and in the offering.
But with the maidservant, He did not make equal
phrases.notes: "He" means the Torah, which set these rules.

phrases.english: neither the man to the woman in lashes,
nor did He make the woman equal to the man in the offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת אֶחָד הָאִישׁ וְאֶחָד הָאִשָּׁה שָׁוִין בַּמַּכּוֹת וּבַקׇּרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second difference to the list started in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With other עריות, the man and the woman are treated the same for מלקות and קרבן. With a שפחה they are not.

steps.title: With other forbidden relations, the first stage counts, and each act brings an offering
steps.stepSummary: With all other עריות, the Torah treats the first stage of the act (מערה) like finishing it (גומר). A person is also חייב a separate offering for every single act.
steps.simpleTranslation: In all forbidden relations, the Torah made one who begins the act like one who finishes it, and a person is liable for each and every act.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a third difference. With the other עריות, just starting the act already makes a person liable, and every act brings its own offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two rules here. First, מערה, the first stage of the act, is enough to be liable, just like finishing. Second, if someone sinned several times by accident, he brings a separate קרבן for each time. The משנה says this about all other עריות, which shows that the שפחה works differently.

keyTerms.meaning: One who does only the first stage of the act
One who finishes the act
Liable; must bring an offering
An act of relations

phrases.english: In all the forbidden relations, He made
one who begins the act like one who finishes it,
and he is liable for each and every act.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הָעֲרָיוֹת עָשָׂה בָּהֶן אֶת הַמְעָרֶה כְּגוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third difference to the list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With other עריות, מערה is like גומר, and each act brings its own offering.

steps.title: Introducing a stringency for the maidservant
steps.stepSummary: The משנה begins to introduce a חומרא, a way the Torah is stricter with the שפחה. The details come in the next part of the text.
steps.simpleTranslation: (This is a stringency:) He was strict with the maidservant,
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. Until now the list showed how other עריות are stricter, and now the משנה turns to show a way the Torah is stricter with the שפחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list so far mostly showed the שפחה as less strict, for example the rule that the first stage counts. Now the direction changes: there is also a חומרא that applies to the שפחה. The details of that חומרא follow right after this line.

keyTerms.meaning: A stringency; a stricter rule
He was strict

phrases.english: (This is a stringency:) He was strict with the maidservant,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ חוֹמֶר הֶחְמִיר בְּשִׁפְחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Changes direction from the differences where other עריות are stricter to a חומרא that applies to the שפחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a way the Torah is stricter with the שפחה. It is spelled out next.
